title: Choose Recall's visual world
question: The roll assigned the Leitner box. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. Every option keeps all features and flows; only the look changes.

options.label: The Leitner Box
options.lineage: the Karteikasten every German student filled before exams
options.thesis: Your courses as real card boxes: watch cards move from 'due' to 'filed' as you learn.
materials: white index-card stock with a red header rule
options.viewport: Box-blue side rail; the dashboard leads with today's box: a huge due count and every course drawn as a box cross-section (Due · New · Filed stacks) on one baseline, Start session on the front.
options.risk: Can tip into skeuomorphic costume if the box drawing grows beyond the data it shows.

raised.raise: One fixed ramp: stack thickness uses the same card-per-pixel scale everywhere, so courses compare honestly.
One shared baseline: all course boxes stand on the same shelf line at the same scale.
Nothing disappears, it is filed: results stamp each card with its rating instead of just listing counts.
Hierarchy by scale contrast: the due count is set very large, labels stay small.
Suspended and archived cards print desaturated in place rather than vanishing.

options.label: Highlighted Lecture Script
options.lineage: the printed Skript, marked up in four highlighter colours the night before the exam
options.thesis: The four ratings are four highlighter inks; progress is literally your material getting marked up.
options.viewport: Clean white workspace; the dashboard's courses are rows whose progress bars are hand-swept highlighter strokes in the rating inks, with the due count highlighted in yellow.
options.risk: Fluorescent inks fight text contrast and can read as a gimmick if strokes go beyond progress and ratings.

options.label: Graphite Console
options.thesis: A graphite study desk where syntax colours mark state and panels persist.
options.viewport: Persistent panels: library on the left, today's queue centre, stats right; syntax-coloured state chips.
options.case: Holds product clarity for an informatics student, but loses on identification: it reads as a dev tool, not a study desk.
options.risk: Drifts toward the hacker look and feels like work software in daylight desk sessions.

options.label: Star Atlas
options.thesis: Mastered cards as brighter stars on a night chart.
options.case: Fuses poorly: obscures the study task and reads dark.
options.kept: A fixed magnitude ramp for mastery.

options.label: Character Goods Catalog
options.thesis: Courses as a roster of mascots.
options.case: Fails a product commitment: no mascots or childish gamification.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.thesis: Cards grow from seed to fruit.
options.case: Fuses poorly: growth metaphor is decorative and lands in the cream-paper rut.
options.kept: Fixed scale on one shared baseline.

options.label: Jet-age Ticket Wallet
options.thesis: A session as a coupon book that tears off card by card.
options.viewport: A ticket wallet for today's session.
options.case: Fuses poorly: travel is foreign to studying.

options.label: Type Specimen
options.case: Fuses poorly: no link to studying.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A modern flashcard app (Anki/Quizlet class), executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar, greeting, stat tiles and a course card grid at full craft.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from other study apps by design.
